properties.description:
`skill_lint.py` walks TOOLS → SKILLS: every served `*_report` must be named in at least one served skill, or carry a written reason in `UNROUTED_REPORTS`. The mirror of the lint's oldest check, which walked skills → tools and caught a skill naming a tool that was gone.

BOTH NEAR-MATCHES READ; THREE KINDS OF RECORD. The fact is the MEASUREMENT of the hole and keeps its own numbers. The ChangeEvent DATES the repair. This is the standing capability that keeps it from reopening — the thing that stays true after the event is history.

WHY THE MIRROR WAS MISSING AND WHAT IT COST. Nothing walked the other way, so a report could be built, correct, verified, and reachable by nobody with every gate green. Measured 2026-08-29: of 14 served reports, SIX were named in no skill — `consumption_report`, `flow_report`, `ility_report`, `maturity_report`, `readiness_report`, `release_report` — and none of the evaluative ones was named in `AGENTS.md` or `service.rs` either. Against the same 23 skills, `detect_gaps` is named 16 times and `loop_status` 12. **The instruction surface was hygiene-weighted, so reflow2 PRESENTED AS a hygiene server while holding nine reports that answer whether a design is actually delivering.**

THE RULE IS A SUFFIX, NOT A LIST. `*_report` is a convention the code already keeps, so it needs no maintenance and cannot silently omit a new report. A hand-kept list of "the evaluative ones" is precisely the thing that rots — the same defect found this morning in `node_ref`, where a judgement made once for one property was never recorded for any other.

THE EXEMPTION REGISTER CARRIES TWO KINDS AND MUST SAY WHICH. `needs no skill` is settled; `GAP:` is a routing hole recorded rather than papered over. Enforced by a test, because the cheap way to pass this check is to name every orphan report in whatever skill is nearest — which satisfies the lint and defeats it. A gap that reads as settled never gets fixed.

🛑 IT CHECKS REACHABILITY, NOT USE. Naming was measured; invocation was not. A report named in a skill is reachable, not necessarily read, and the 93-session skill-adoption result says what predicts use is an always-injected surface — which a skill is not. This closes the unreachable half and leaves the unread half open.
properties.name: A report nobody is routed to fails the build, or says in writing why it needs no route
